subject: QBR prep: release assurance & timeline triage for May launch
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: release assurance & timeline triage for May launch

Team —

We need a concise status and risk triage ahead of next week's QBR prep slot (Thu 12th). Nimbus Health is sticking to the week-of-May-11 production cutover; they want our final runbook and a confirmed contingency plan. Please send an updated one-page status by EOD Monday with the following:

- Current gate status (code freeze, infra readiness, external approvals)
- Top 3 delivery risks and mitigations we can present to the QBR audience
- Any ask of Leadership (credits, extra DRI headcount, schedule buffer)

I've attached the latest timeline and risk register — feel free to update the sheet directly in Drive. We'll synthesize for the exec deck.

Quick notes: Nimbus flagged latency regressions in their perf harness last week (their Ops gave a short log excerpt). We need confirmation on the KV cache rollout plan and whether the canary window can be extended.

Sergio
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: launch_timeline_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), release_risk_register_20260305.csv (csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: release assurance & timeline triage for May launch

Sergio — thanks for the ping. High-level update below; I'll attach a one-pager into the Drive folder by EOD Monday as requested.

Gate status
- Code freeze: target 2026-04-20. Engineering currently has two critical PRs open (model-delta and batching fix).
- Infra readiness: Dedicated pool provisioning on track; need final IP allowlist from Nimbus (pending).
- External approvals: Nimbus legal requested a short amendment to data retention terms — working w/ sales and legal.

Top risks (short)
1) Latency regression in customer perf harness — root cause appears related to a model variant mismatch and KV cache misses. Mitigation: delayed variant rollout + extended KV warm-up window; engineering can add an opt-in caching prewarm in the canary.
2) Approval/contract redline lag — if legal takes >10 business days we need to push the cutover. Ask: brief exec escalation to Nimbus legal contact if needed.
3) Infra capacity boundary cases during sustained peak — mitigation: warm spare on Dedicated pool for two weeks post-cutover (cost impact estimate attached).

Asks for leadership: permission to hold a one-time warm-spare credit for the cutover week (estimate in spreadsheet) and guidance on an accelerated legal escalation if negotiation stalls.

I'll update the risk register with the root-cause notes and estimated impact bands. More from Tessa on engineering specifics.

Laura
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: release assurance & timeline triage for May launch

Adding engineering detail and explicit mitigation options. I've updated the risk register (see attachment) and annotated the timeline sheet.

Technical summary
- Latency regression: traced to model-delta handler that misroutes a small percentage (~3%) of requests to the larger fp32 variant when the q8 variant's KV entries are aged out. This shows as a 70–120ms p95 uplift in Nimbus's harness.
- Root cause: race in variant-selection logic under eviction pressure + lack of proactive KV prewarm for long-tail prefixes.

Mitigation options (ordered by risk reduction vs effort)
A) Short-term (2–3 days): Force- pin the canary to q8-only for Nimbus, extend canary from 48h -> 96h, add proactive KV prewarm job before canary traffic. Low dev effort, quick rollback path.
B) Medium-term (2 weeks): Fix race in variant-selection logic and add a lightweight background KV rehydrate. Medium dev effort; will eliminate the intermittent misroute.
C) Long-term (6+ weeks): Rework eviction policy + refactor selection to deterministic fallback matrix. High effort but the most robust.

Canary and rollout ask
- Recommend option A for QBR presentation: we can present the canary extension + forced q8 pin as a confident mitigation.
- Need ops: permit a 96-hour canary window and an extra dedicated instance (warm-spare) for the first 72 hours of production. Ops cost estimate in spreadsheet.

Attachments: release_risk_register_20260305.csv (updated)

Tessa
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick summary for the QBR notes and the exec thread to Nimbus:

- We propose Option A (q8 pin + extend canary to 96h + proactive KV prewarm) as the immediate mitigation.
- We are asking Nimbus to approve a 72-hour warm-spare (ops capacity) window post-cutover and to expedite IP allowlist + legal minor amendment.

Nora — looping you in so your product/ops team can confirm whether the 96h canary and warm-spare are acceptable, and whether Nimbus can get the IP allowlist to us this week. If legal needs a direct contact, Vivek can coordinate.

Next steps:
- Laura/Tessa: I'll take the one-pager and the annotated risk register to synthesize a 3-slide QBR section by Wed EOD.
- Vivek: please advise if we should propose a compensation credit or absorb the warm-spare, and whether you want me to escalate to Nimbus execs.

I'll hold off on external communication until I have Nora's confirmation here.

Sergio
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
